title: Gulf states press US to neutralise Iran for good as Hormuz crisis deepens – report
byline: Gulf Arab states did not ask the U.S. to go to war with Iran, but many are now urging it not to stop short by leaving the Islamic Republic still able to threaten the Gulf’s oil lifeline and the economies that depend on it, three Gulf sources told Reuters.

title: UAE temporarily closes airspace amid missile and drone threats from Iran
byline: The United Arab Emirates’ air defences are responding to incoming missile and drone threats from Iran, Reuters reports.

title: US embassy in Iraq targeted by drone strikes
byline: The US embassy in Baghdad has been targeted by a wave of drone and rocket attacks, according to reports from Reuters and Agence France-Presse (AFP).

title: Trump seeks to delay China summit due to Iran war
byline: US President Donald Trump said on Monday that he is planning to delay a high stakes visit to China later in March by about a month because of the Iran war.

title: Showers expected in parts of the island today
byline: Showers or thundershowers will occur at several places in Central, Sabaragamuwa, Southern and Uva provinces after 2.00 pm, today (17), the Department of Meteorology said.

title: Government schools to close on Wednesdays amid fuel shortage
byline: The Secretary to the Ministry of Education, Nalaka Kaluwewe, has announced that all government schools will remain closed on Wednesdays due to the ongoing fuel supply crisis.

title: Trump upset as US partners reject call for Hormuz warship escorts
byline: Several U.S. allies rebuffed Donald Trump’s call on Monday to send warships to escort tankers through the Strait of Hormuz, drawing criticism from the U.S. president, who accused Western partners of ingratitude after decades of support.

title: Iran navy chief vows ‘deadly’ response for IRIS Dena ship sinking
byline: Iran’s navy commander Shahram Irani warned that Tehran’s enemies would face retaliation for the killing of dozens of sailors after the IRIS Dena was sunk in the Indian Ocean off Sri Lanka.

title: Wednesdays declared holidays for tuition classes
byline: Due to ongoing fuel supply challenges, the Commissioner General of Essential Services, Prabath Chandrakeerthi, has requested not to conduct tuition classes on Wednesdays.

title: Russia urges end to Middle East hostilities, condemns US-Israel actions
byline: The Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Monday issued a strong statement condemning the recent escalation of violence in the Middle East blaming the United States and Israel for what it described as a ‘‘treacherous and unprovoked attack on Iran’‘ and calling for an immediate end to hostilities.

title: Govt’s objective is to create opportunities for all citizens to enjoy freedom – PM
byline: Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya stated that freedom had long been limited to only a privileged segment of society and that the government’s objective is to create opportunities for all citizens to equally experience and enjoy that freedom.

title: Selected Health Ministry Departments to work from home on Wednesdays
byline: In light of the prevailing global crisis and in line with government measures to minimize fuel consumption, the Ministry of Health has authorized officers in selected sectors to work from home every Wednesday.

title: Afghanistan says 400 killed in Pakistan air strike on Kabul hospital, Pakistan rejects claim
byline: At least 400 people were killed and 250 injured in an air strike by Pakistan on a drug users rehabilitation hospital in Kabul, a spokesman of the Afghan Taliban government said on Tuesday, a sharp escalation in the conflict between the neighbours.

title: Air traffic resumes in UAE, state media says
byline: Air traffic operations have returned to normal in the United Arab Emirates after a temporary closure earlier on Tuesday, state media is reporting, as cited by Reuters.

title: Trump was warned of likely Iranian retaliation on Gulf allies, sources say
byline: President Donald Trump was warned that attacking Iran could trigger retaliation against U.S. Gulf allies despite his claims on Monday that Tehran’s reaction came as a surprise, said a U.S. official and two sources familiar with U.S. intelligence reports.

title: Only one vehicle can be registered for QR system per NIC and phone number – Official
byline: The Ministry of Digital Economy has confirmed that, under a new policy decision, only one vehicle can be registered under each National Identity Card (NIC) number and telephone number through the QR code system.

title: Weekly fuel quota valid until midnight every Saturday – CPC Chairman
byline: The Chairman of the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC), D.J. Rajakaruna, announced that the weekly fuel quota issued to the public under the QR code–based system will remain valid until 12 midnight on Saturday every week and will be refreshed every Sunday.

title: Energy Minister warns of possible power cuts amid fuel crisis in Sri Lanka
byline: Minister of Energy, Kumara Jayakodi, stated that although no power cuts have been implemented thus far despite the ongoing fuel crisis, there is a possibility that such measures may be required in the future.

title: Google Maps reinvents navigation with AI-powered ‘Ask Maps’
byline: Google Maps just got a major upgrade that could make the world’s most popular navigation app even better.

title: Pre-schools to remain closed on Wednesdays; Private schools requested to do same
byline: The Ministry of Education stated that, as government schools are closed on Wednesdays which have been declared as public holidays, a request has been made for government-approved private schools to also remain closed on those days.

title: Advisory issued for severe lightning
byline: An ‘Amber’ advisory has been issued by the Department of Meteorology for severe lightning in the Western and Sabaragamuwa provinces and in Kandy, Nuwara-Eliya, Monaragala, Galle and Matara districts.

title: Parliament sitting cancelled tomorrow
byline: Taking into consideration the declaration of every Wednesday as a public holiday due to the prevailing situation, it has been decided that the Parliament of Sri Lanka will not convene tomorrow (18).

title: Energy Minister provides update on existing fuel supplies
byline: Minister of Energy, Kumara Jayakodi, made a statement in Parliament today (17) regarding the duration for which fuel supplies are sufficient in the country under normal consumption.

title: Man nabbed while transporting stock of fuel in three-wheeler
byline: An individual has been arrested in Bandaragama for illegally transporting a stock of fuel in a three-wheeler.

title: Ex-President Gotabaya leaves Bribery Commission after recording statement
byline: UPDATE: Former President Gotabaya Rajapaksa has left the Bribery Commission after giving a statement regarding an ongoing investigation.

title: Three committees appointed to safeguard Sri Lanka’s economy amid Middle East crisis - PM
byline: Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya announced in Parliament today (17) that three committees have been appointed to manage potential economic challenges Sri Lanka may face in light of the ongoing war situation in the Middle East, with steps already underway to implement the necessary measures in this regard.

title: President to hold special press conference tonight
byline: Minister Bimal Rathnayake stated that President Anura Kumara Dissanayake is scheduled to hold a special press conference tonight (17) concerning the current situation in Sri Lanka.

title: New circular issued revising public service schedule to conserve fuel
byline: The Ministry of Public Administration, Provincial Councils and Local Government has issued a circular regarding the continuation of government office operations in order to conserve fuel reserves, amidst the prevailing crisis situation in the country.

title: Five Chinese nationals arrested at BIA with cigarettes and used phones worth Rs. 18 million
byline: Five Chinese nationals have been arrested by Customs officials at the Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA) in the early hours today (17) for attempting to smuggle a consignment of foreign-manufactured cigarettes and used mobile phones valued at around Rs. 18 million into the country.

title: Public transport services, including trains, to be limited on Wednesdays
byline: Public transport services, including train operations, will be limited on Wednesdays, which have been declared as government holidays, according to Cabinet Spokesman Nalinda Jayatissa.

title: Sri Lanka sets up four committees to mitigate issues due to Middle East conflict
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has granted approval to the proposal submitted by the President to establish four committees to provide suitable recommendations on immediate measures needed to minimize the adverse impacts on the local economy and public life caused by the conflict in the Middle East.

title: Israel says Iran’s key security chief Larijani has been killed in strike
byline: Defence Minister Israel Katz said on Tuesday the Israeli military had killed Iran’s security chief and the head of its Basij militia in airstrikes overnight. Larijani is a former nuclear negotiator and a close ally of slain supreme leader Ali Khamenei.

title: Guidelines to maintain school activities amid fuel crisis; no parades, school trips
byline: In response to the ongoing global fuel crisis, the Ministry of Education has introduced several measures and guidelines to ensure the uninterrupted continuation of school administrative functions and teaching activities while minimizing energy consumption.

title: ‘Avurudu Nekath Seettuwa’ for Sinhala and Tamil New Year released
byline: The government has released the ‘Avurudu Nekath Seettuwa’ for this year’s Sinhala and Tamil New Year.

title: Most issues with fuel QR system resolved, says Cabinet Spokesperson
byline: Most of the issues related to the QR code system used for obtaining fuel have been resolved, the Cabinet Spokesperson Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa has stated.

title: Israel targets Iran’s Supreme National Security Council Chief Ali Larijani
byline: Israel targeted Ali Larijani, the head of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, in a Tehran strike on Monday night, according to an Israeli Military spokesperson.

title: Global jet fuel, diesel prices poised to surge more than crude as Iran war rages: Report
byline: The disruption in the global oil market triggered by the ongoing Iran war, which has engulfed the entire Middle East, is poised to have a greater impact on products such as jet fuel and diesel than on crude, according to a Goldman Sachs Group report.

title: Multi-day fishing trawler seized with heroin off Dondra: Female owner and son arrested
byline: The female owner of the multi-day fishing trawler seized off Dondra while transporting a haul of narcotics and her son have been arrested on suspicion of aiding and abetting a drug trafficking operation.

title: Tomorrow’s parliamentary sitting cancelled
byline: Taking into consideration the declaration of every Wednesday as a public holiday due to the prevailing situation, it has been decided that the Parliament of Sri Lanka will not convene tomorrow (18).

title: Public urged to report filling stations bypassing QR system
byline: The law is being strictly enforced regarding filling stations dispensing fuel outside the QR system, and steps are being taken to suspend their licenses, the Chairman of the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC), D.J. Rajakaruna stated.

title: Fraud case against Udaya Gammanpila to be recalled on March 27
byline: The Colombo High Court has ordered that the case filed against former Minister Udaya Gammanpila, who is accused of misappropriating company shares worth Rs. 20 million belonging to an Australian businessman by preparing a forged Power of Attorney, be recalled on March 27, 2026.

title: Amazon launches 1-hour shipping in US cities to challenge Walmart
byline: Amazon is ramping up its speedy delivery service by offering 1-hour and 3-hour shipping in markets across the U.S., including Los Angeles and Chicago, in its latest efforts to stave off e-commerce competition from its biggest rival Walmart.

title: Minister assures continuous fuel supply for industries
byline: The government is operating under a special system to ensure an uninterrupted fuel supply for the industrial sector, the Minister of Industry and Entrepreneurship Development, Sunil Handunneththi has stated.

title: Another fuel ship arrives in Colombo amid energy crisis
byline: Another fuel shipment ordered by Sri Lanka has arrived at the Colombo Port, amid the energy crisis caused by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, the Ministry of Ports and Civil Aviation have confirmed.

title: PUCSL’s Western Province public consultation on proposed electricity tariff revision tomorrow
byline: The final provincial public consultation session for verbal submissions on the proposal submitted by the Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB) to revise electricity tariffs for the second quarter of 2026 will be held in Colombo tomorrow (18) by the Public Utilities Commission of Sri Lanka (PUCSL).

title: Sri Lanka assures seamless travel experience for tourists
byline: Sri Lanka remains fully open and ready to welcome international visitors, ensuring a safe and seamless travel experience across the island, the Sri Lanka Tourism Promotion Bureau has announced.

title: President directs all Ministries and officials to conserve fuel
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake emphasised that each Ministry must have a practical plan in place for fuel conservation, noting that it should be a sustainable, data-driven process that ensures minimal energy consumption.

title: Warm weather advisory issued for several provinces for tomorrow
byline: A warm weather advisory has been issued for residents of the Western, Sabaragamuwa, Southern and North-Western provinces and in the Monaragala, Mannar, Vavuniya, and Anuradhapura districts.

title: Iran says it seized hundreds of Starlink terminals, state media reports
byline: Iran’s Ministry of Intelligence claimed that it seized hundreds of Starlink satellite internet systems in a nationwide operation, according to Iranian state media on Tuesday.

title: Iran war may push 45 million people into acute hunger by June, WFP says
byline: Tens of millions more people will face acute hunger if the Iran war continues through to June, according to analysis from the World Food Programme released on Tuesday.

title: 134 foreign nationals arrested following raid on Chinese-led online scam centres in Sri Lanka
byline: A total of 134 foreign nationals, including 126 Chinese nationals, four from Myanmar, and four Taiwanese, were arrested during a joint operation conducted by Sri Lanka Army intelligence units and the Department of Immigration and Emigration.

title: 33,000 MT of Litro LP gas shipment due in Sri Lanka within two days
byline: A stock of 38,000 MT of Litro LP gas has already arrived this month and another 33,000 MT are expected within two days, said President Anura Kumara Dissanayake while addressing a special media briefing.

title: Train services to operate on Saturday’s schedule tomorrow – SLR
byline: Railway services will be operated tomorrow (Wednesday) as on a Saturday, as it is a government declared holiday, according to Sri Lanka Railways.
